rows.method: mVMC with SU(2) and symmetry projections

compute.reported_as: Exploiting the SU(2) symmetry of the model [50-53], we keep up to 20000 SU(2) states, (typically equivalent to >~ 80000 U(1) states). [...] For small bond dimensions (chi <~ 2000) we use the two-site version of the DMRG, and switch to the one-site variant to optimize the wave function for larger chi. [...] It turns out that even the calculation of the two-site variance becomes too costly for clusters with more than ~ 100 sites and bond dimensions >~ 8000. In certain cases, we revert to the usage of the two-site DMRG and extrapolate as a function of the truncation error (cf. 108-site cluster). [...] FIG. 5. [...] The corresponding maximal bond dimensions for the 32, 64, 108 and 128-site clusters are 20000, 16000, 16000 and 12000 respectively. [...] Some of the data presented here was produced using the SyTen toolkit, originally created by Claudius Hubig.
compute.source: Hagymasi, Schaefer, Moessner & Luitz, Phys. Rev. Lett. 126, 117204 (2021) = arXiv:2010.03563: 'Model and methods'; Fig. 5 caption; Acknowledgments, arXiv:2010.03563 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: bond_dimension = 16000 is the maximal SU(2) bond dimension stated for the 108-site cluster (Fig. 5 caption); the paper's SU(2) states are 'typically equivalent to >~ 80000 U(1) states' at chi = 20000. The 108-site energy was obtained with two-site DMRG and extrapolated in the truncation error (Table I: -0.4935(50) per site extrapolated; the worklist energy corresponds to -0.4851 per site in S-units, i.e. presumably a finite-chi variational value quoted by a later paper rather than the extrapolated value). No CPU hours, core count, wall-clock or machine stated; acknowledgments list only funding and the SyTen toolkit. Worklist had no arXiv id; arXiv 2010.03563 read from the repo cache.
